mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes GLC 250 or 300 petrol engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt M274 engine for the GLC 250 costs £2,500-£4,000 supply-only; a rebuilt M264 engine for the GLC 300 costs £3,200-£4,500 supply-only. Fitting adds £800-£1,500 depending on complexity.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure on a Mercedes GLC 250/300 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: A 1-3 second rattling noise on cold start is the classic warning - most common on M274 petrol engines (GLC 250/300, 2015-2019). Ignoring it risks engine seizure and £5,000+ repair bills.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes GLC 300 petrol (M264) reliable? What are the common problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M264 is a modern, efficient engine with strong performance, but has a known cylinder head exhaust valve failure that can occur as early as 40,000 miles - causing misfire and sudden power loss. The 48V mild-hybrid system also adds complexity.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes GLC 250/300 petrol engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly maintained M274 petrol engines routinely reach 150,000-200,000 miles before major work. The M264 is too new for definitive long-term data, but early indications suggest similar longevity with proper maintenance - assuming the cylinder head issue is addressed.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes GLC 250 or 300 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the GLC is otherwise in good condition with no rust or major electrical faults. A rebuilt M274 costs £2,500-£4,000 - far less than replacing a £14,000-£38,000 vehicle. The GLC's strong residual values make engine replacement financially justifiable.

mainEntity.name: What oil does my Mercedes GLC 250 or 300 petrol need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mercedes-Benz specifies MB 229.5 high-performance oil for the M274 and M264 - typically 5W-30 or 5W-40 fully synthetic. The M274 requires approximately 6.5 litres; the M264 requires approximately 6.1-7.0 litres.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz GLC Class 250/300 Petrol - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The GLC 250 and 300 petrol models launched alongside the X253 GLC in 2015, offering the M274 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder with 211hp and 245hp respectively. In 2019, the facelift brought the M264 with EQ Boost mild-hybrid technology - more power, better efficiency, and the 48V belt-driven starter-generator that changed how these engines are serviced and repaired.

milestones.description: M264.920, 2.0L turbo petrol with 48V EQ Boost, 197hp (GLC 200, facelift X253) / 258hp (GLC 300, facelift X253)
X254 second-generation launched; GLC 300 continues with M254, GLC 250 badge retired

items.title: 2.0L Turbo Petrol (2015-2019)
items.commonFailure: Timing chain tensioner wear and camshaft adjuster (phaser) failure - cold-start rattle is the classic warning sign. Timing chain lifespan is approximately 80,000 miles (plus or minus 20,000 miles). Camshaft adjuster wear typically begins around 60,000-70,000 miles. The M274 also suffers from thermostat failure (labour-intensive to replace) and, at higher mileages, turbocharger failure.

items.title: 2.0L Turbo Petrol with 48V EQ Boost (2019-2025)
items.commonFailure: Cylinder head / exhaust valve failure - misfire and sudden power loss reported as early as 40,000 miles. The M264 also suffers from 48V BSG (belt-driven starter-generator) issues; the BSG is belt-driven off the crankshaft, combining starter, generator and regenerative braking functions. Though some sources suggest the GLC's M264 did not receive the 48V system in all markets, UK-spec facelift X253 models with M264 are 48V-equipped.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz GLC Class 250/300 Petrol Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The GLC 250 and 300 petrol models are powered by two generations of the same 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder - the M274 (2015-2019) and the M264 (2019-2025). Both are fundamentally strong engines, but each has well-documented weak points. The M274 is known for timing chain tensioner wear and camshaft adjuster rattle. The M264 introduced 48V mild-hybrid complexity and has a known cylinder head exhaust valve failure. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.group: M274 Timing Chain & Camshaft Adjuster Failure
problems.h4: M274 Timing Chain & Camshaft Adjuster Failure - The Cold-Start Rattle
problems.rootCause: The camshaft adjusters (phasers) wear internally, and the timing chain stretches over time. Cold-start rattle - a 1-3 second rattling noise on startup - is the classic warning sign. If ignored, timing can jump, causing valve contact and catastrophic engine failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain tensioner only - valid if caught immediately when rattle first appears
repairOptions.longevity: Effective only if addressed within first 500 miles of noise

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides, camshaft sprockets. Labour-intensive (8-10 hours).
Replace both bank camshaft adjusters (phasers), reseal timing covers
repairOptions.longevity: If rattle is from adjusters, not chain stretch

repairOptions.tier: Full Replacement - Rebuilt M274 engine with updated components
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M274 engine with updated tensioner and camshaft adjusters
repairOptions.longevity: If timing has jumped causing valve damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2015-2019 GLC 250 or 300 petrol 4MATIC is worth approximately £14,000-£28,000 depending on mileage and condition. The GLC 250/300 sits in the £15,000+ band - replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value, making a full rebuilt engine a justifiable investment for owners planning to keep the car. For higher-mileage examples approaching the £8,000-£15,000 band, evaluate both options carefully.
problems.recommendation: If you hear the characteristic 2-3 second rattle only on cold start with no fault codes, replace the tensioner immediately - it's £300-500 well spent. Once chain skip triggers camshaft correlation codes (P0016/P0017), the full timing kit is mandatory. If the engine has jumped timing causing valve contact, only a full replacement engine makes financial sense. For camshaft adjuster rattle, replace both adjusters simultaneously - doing one bank alone invites a repeat workshop visit within months.

problems.group: M264 Cylinder Head / Exhaust Valve Failure
problems.h4: M264 Cylinder Head / Exhaust Valve Failure - The Facelift Petrol Concern
problems.rootCause: A defective exhaust valve in the cylinder head can fail, causing a catastrophic misfire and sudden loss of power. This is a known issue affecting M264 engines, with multiple owner reports of failures just outside factory warranty.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Compression and leakdown test to confirm cylinder head failure
repairOptions.longevity: First step - confirms whether head replacement is needed

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace cylinder head with updated casting, new exhaust valves, gaskets
repairOptions.longevity: If caught before bottom-end damage occurs

repairOptions.tier: Full Replacement - Rebuilt M264 engine with updated head
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M264 engine with updated cylinder head, new timing components, 48V system recalibration
repairOptions.longevity: If valve failure has caused piston or bore damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2019-2025 GLC 300 petrol 4MATIC is worth approximately £20,000-£38,000 depending on mileage and condition. The GLC 300 sits firmly in the £15,000+ band - replacement cost is modest relative to vehicle value. However, the cylinder head failure can occur at relatively low mileage; if caught early, head replacement alone is the value play.
problems.recommendation: If you experience misfire, sudden power loss, or a whistling noise from the engine on your M264-powered GLC 300, have a compression test performed immediately. If cylinder head failure is confirmed and caught before metal debris has contaminated the oil system, head replacement alone is the right call - ensure the specialist uses the updated cylinder head casting. If the engine has been driven with the misfire or if oil pressure has dropped, a full rebuilt engine is the only safe option. Check whether your vehicle is still within warranty - some M264 cylinder head repairs have been covered under goodwill from Mercedes.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M264 Mercedes GLC 300 petrol engine prices

problems.group: M274 Excessive Oil Consumption & Thermostat Failure
problems.h4: M274 Excessive Oil Consumption & Thermostat Failure - The Hidden Cost Traps
problems.rootCause: Piston ring wear leads to excessive oil consumption on higher-mileage M274 engines. The thermostat (housed in a complex assembly under the engine) fails, causing slow warm-up and poor fuel economy - replacement requires approximately 3 hours of labour.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace thermostat assembly, drain and refill coolant
repairOptions.longevity: If slow warm-up or cooling system warning

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Strip engine, replace piston rings, hone cylinders
repairOptions.longevity: If oil consumption exceeds 1L per 1,000 miles

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M274 engine with updated piston rings and thermostat
repairOptions.longevity: If oil consumption has caused bore scoring

problems.vehicleValueCheck: As above - a typical GLC 250/300 petrol is worth £14,000-£28,000.
problems.recommendation: The thermostat is a known weak point on the M274 - if you notice the engine taking longer than usual to reach operating temperature or the temperature gauge fluctuating, budget £350-£550 for replacement. For oil consumption, monitor your oil level between services - Mercedes allows up to 0.8L per 1,000km (approximately 0.8L per 620 miles). If consumption exceeds this, have a compression test performed. If piston rings are the cause and the engine is otherwise healthy, ring replacement is viable. If bore scoring is present, a full rebuilt engine is the only lasting solution.
